s:
Match List-I (Battle) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Kasahrada (Kayadara) near Mount Abu | i. 1191
b. First Battle of Tarain | ii. 1178
c. Second Battle of Tarain | iii. 1192
d. Battle of Chandawar | iv. 1194
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kasahrada – 1178 (Mularaja II beat Ghori, his first defeat); First Tarain – 1191 (Prithviraj won); Second Tarain – 1192 (Ghori won); Chandawar – 1194 (Ghori, army under Aibak, beat Jaichand).

s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Ghori's battles:
1. Ghori's first defeat came in 1178 at Kasahrada near Mount Abu during his Gujarat campaign.
2. Mularaja II's queen mother Naika Devi acted as regent at that time.
3. The Battle of Chandawar was fought near Karnal in Haryana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Chandawar (1194) was fought near Firozabad (UP) on the Yamuna; it is Tarain that lies near Karnal, Haryana.

s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Ghori:
1. He entered India by the Khyber Pass.
2. His first Indian invasion (1175) was against Multan.
3. He took Punjab and Lahore in 1186 from Khusru Malik, the last Ghaznavid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Ghori entered India by the Gomal Pass.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Battles of Tarain:
1. The First Battle of Tarain arose over Ghori's attack on Tabarhinda (Bhatinda).
2. In the Second Battle, Jaichand of Kannauj sent troops to help Prithviraj.
3. The Turkish cavalry speed and mounted archery beat the larger Rajput army in 1192.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: Jaichand refused to help Prithviraj in 1192.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni's raids, Muhammad Ghori's invasions led to lasting Turkish rule in North India.
Reason (R): Ghori aimed at conquest and permanent occupation, and left his slave Aibak as his representative in India.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: Ghori sought conquest and permanent occupation (Mahmud only plundered), and Aibak, his representative after 1192, became the first Sultan in 1206.

s:
Consider the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak:
1. He was a slave of Muhammad Ghori and held the post of Master of Stables.
2. He became the first Sultan when Ghori died near Jhelum in 1206.
3. His capital as the first Sultan was Delhi.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 2) are correct. 3 is wrong: Aibak's capital was Lahore.

s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad bin Qasim:
1. He was the nephew and son-in-law of Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf, the Umayyad governor of Iraq.
2. He was sent to Sindh by Caliph Harun al-Rashid.
3. The capital of Raja Dahir, whom he defeated, was Alor (Aror).
4. Debal, Sehwan and Somnath were among the places he took.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: he was sent by Caliph al-Walid. 4 is wrong: he took Debal, Nirun, Sehwan, Brahmanabad and Multan – Somnath was Mahmud's raid of 1025.

s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author / translator):
List-I | List-II
a. Chachnama (Persian translation) | i. Al-Biladuri
b. Futuh al-Buldan | ii. Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi
c. Muruj-ul-Zehab | iii. Al-Masudi
d. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri | iv. Minhaj-us-Siraj
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Chachnama (13th-century Persian translation) – Kufi; Futuh al-Buldan – Al-Biladuri (9th c.); Muruj-ul-Zehab – Al-Masudi (10th c.); Tabaqat-i-Nasiri – Minhaj-us-Siraj.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Arab conquest of Sindh:
1. Piracy against Arab ships was one of its causes.
2. It was followed by mass Islamisation of the Hindus and Buddhists of Sindh.
3. Through it Indian decimal and place-value mathematics reached the Islamic world and then Europe.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: there was no mass Islamisation; Hindus and Buddhists were given dhimmi status.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Arab rule in India remained confined to Sindh and Multan.
Reason (R): Nagabhata I of the Rashtrakuta dynasty drove the Arabs back.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: the Thar and Aravallis, strong Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas and Palas and weak Arab resources confined them. R is false: Nagabhata I was a Pratihara, not a Rashtrakuta.

s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Role):
List-I | List-II
a. Alptigin | i. Hindu Shahi ruler who fought at Waihind
b. Sabuktigin | ii. Founder of the Ghaznavid dynasty
c. Mahmud | iii. Seventeen raids on India, 1000-1027
d. Anandapala | iv. Seized Ghazni in 962 as a Samanid slave-general
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Alptigin only seized Ghazni (962) under the Samanids; Sabuktigin (977-997) founded the dynasty; Mahmud made 17 raids (1000-1027); Anandapala (Hindu Shahi) fought Mahmud at Waihind (1008-09).

s:
Match List-I (Raid of Mahmud of Ghazni) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Nagarkot (Kangra) | i. 1009
b. Thanesar (Chakraswamin temple) | ii. 1025
c. Kanauj, where the Pratihara king submitted | iii. 1014
d. Somnath | iv. 1018
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Nagarkot – 1009; Thanesar – 1014; Mathura and Kanauj – 1018 (the Pratihara king submitted); Somnath – 1025-26.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mahmud raided Somnath in 1025 when the Solanki Bhima I ruled Gujarat.
2. Bhima I reconstructed the Somnath temple after Mahmud left.
3. The Chandela Vidyadhara was defeated by Mahmud in 1019.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 2) are correct. 3 is wrong: Vidyadhara faced Mahmud in 1019 and 1022 and was not defeated – peace was made.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. After Mahmud the Ghaznavids declined under Seljuk pressure.
2. Mahmud's title Yamini-ud-Daulah was given by the Fatimid caliph.
3. Muhammad Ghori ended the Ghaznavid dynasty in 1186.
4. The Somnath Swabhiman Parv (January 2026) marks 1,000 years since Mahmud's attack on Somnath.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: Yamini-ud-Daulah came from the Abbasid caliph (hence 'Yamini dynasty').

s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Kitab Patanjal | i. Al-Biruni
b. Kitab-ul-Yamini | ii. Baihaqi
c. Tarikh-i-Subuktigin | iii. Hasan Nizami
d. Taj-ul-Maasir | iv. Utbi
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kitab Patanjal (Arabic Yoga-Sutra) – Al-Biruni; Kitab-ul-Yamini – Utbi; Tarikh-i-Subuktigin – Baihaqi; Taj-ul-Maasir – Hasan Nizami (Ghurid era).

s:
Consider the following statements about Mahmud of Ghazni's court:
1. Firdausi, called the 'Homer of the East', wrote the Shahnama.
2. Unsuri was the poet laureate (Malik-ush-Shuara).
3. Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by H.G. Raverty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by Edward Sachau.

s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of Turkish success:
1. North India lacked political unity after the collapse of the Pratiharas.
2. The Turks relied on mobile cavalry and mounted archers against elephant-reliant armies.
3. R.S. Sharma linked Turkish success to 'Indian feudalism'.
4. Ghori's army at Tarain in 1192 was larger than Prithviraj's.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 3) are correct. 4 is wrong: Prithviraj's army was the larger one; the Turks won by superior war technique and organisation.

s:
Consider the following statements about Bakhtiyar Khalji:
1. He was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar.
2. He entered Nadiya in 1204 and drove Lakshmana Sena to East Bengal.
3. His Tibet expedition of 1205 was a success.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: his Tibet expedition of 1205 failed, and he was killed in 1206. He ruled from Lakhnauti.

s:
Match List-I (Solanki ruler) with List-II (Contribution):
List-I | List-II
a. Mularaja I | i. Built the Modhera Sun temple
b. Bhima I | ii. Rebuilt the Somnath temple in stone
c. Jayasimha Siddharaja | iii. Founded the dynasty with capital at Anhilwada
d. Kumarapala | iv. Built the Sahasralinga tank at Patan
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Mularaja I (c. 940) – founder, capital Anhilwada; Bhima I – Modhera Sun temple; Jayasimha Siddharaja – Sahasralinga tank at Patan and patron of Hemachandra; Kumarapala – Jain disciple of Hemachandra who rebuilt Somnath in stone.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Dilwara temples at Mount Abu:
1. The Vimal Vasahi was built c. 1031 by Vimal Shah, minister of Bhima I.
2. The Vimal Vasahi is dedicated to Neminatha.
3. The Luna Vasahi was built in 1230 by the Vaghela ministers Vastupala and Tejpal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Vimal Vasahi is dedicated to Rishabha (Adinatha); Neminatha is the deity of Luna Vasahi.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Somnath temple:
1. It is a Vaishnava shrine.
2. The 'Old Somnath' temple was built by Ahilyabai Holkar in 1783.
3. The present temple was built in 1947.
4. It is built in the Dravida style.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only one (2) is correct. 1 is wrong: Somnath is a Shiva jyotirlinga. 3 is wrong: the present temple was built in 1951. 4 is wrong: its style is Maru-Gurjara (a Nagara sub-style), not Dravida.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Kumarapala sent his ministers to stop cruelty to animals in the Kashi region.
Reason (R): Kumarapala was a Jain and a disciple of Hemachandra.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: as a Jain disciple of Hemachandra, Kumarapala curbed animal killing, even sending ministers to stop cruelty to animals in Kashi.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chandelas:
1. Their founder Nannuka claimed Agnikula origin.
2. Khajuraho, Mahoba and Kalanjar were their centres.
3. The Khajuraho group of temples is in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh.
4. The Kandariya Mahadeva temple, dedicated to Shiva, was built by Vidyadhara.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (2, 3 and 4) are correct. 1 is wrong: the Chandelas claimed moon descent (Chandratreya), not Agnikula origin.

s:
Match List-I (Work / monument) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. Samarangana Sutradhara | i. An unfinished Shiva temple
b. Saraswati-Kanthabharana | ii. Life of the Paramara Sindhuraja
c. Navasahasanka Charita | iii. Architecture and mechanical devices (yantras)
d. Bhojeshwar temple, Bhojpur | iv. Poetics and grammar
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Samarangana Sutradhara (Bhoja) – architecture, town planning and yantras; Saraswati-Kanthabharana (Bhoja) – poetics and grammar; Navasahasanka Charita (Padmagupta) – Sindhuraja; Bhojeshwar temple (Raisen) – unfinished Shiva temple beside Bhojtal.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhojshala at Dhar:
1. It was a temple of Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi).
2. Muslims call it the Kamal Maula Mosque.
3. An ASI survey of it was ordered in 2022.
4. In May 2026 the Rajasthan High Court declared it a Hindu temple.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 2) are correct. 3 is wrong: the ASI survey was ordered in 2024. 4 is wrong: it was the Madhya Pradesh High Court.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Paramaras of Malwa:
1. The dynasty was founded by Upendra (Krishnaraja), a Rashtrakuta feudatory.
2. Bhoja moved the capital from Dhara to Ujjain.
3. The last ruler, Mahalakadeva, was killed in 1305 by Alauddin Khalji's forces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Bhoja moved the capital from Ujjain to Dhara (Dhar).

s:
Match List-I (Dynasty) with List-II (Founder):
List-I | List-II
a. Chahamana (Chauhan) | i. Kokalla I
b. Tomara | ii. Anangapala
c. Gahadavala | iii. Vasudeva
d. Kalachuri (Chedi) | iv. Chandradeva
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Chahamana – Vasudeva; Tomara – Anangapala (Dhillika); Gahadavala – Chandradeva (1089); Kalachuri – Kokalla I (Tripuri).

s:
Consider the following statements about theories of Rajput origin:
1. Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith proposed a foreign origin.
2. G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya held that the Rajputs were of Kshatriya descent.
3. The Agnikula clans of Chand Bardai include the Chandelas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the four Agnikula clans are the Pratiharas, Chaulukyas (Solankis), Paramaras and Chahamanas; the Chandelas claimed lunar descent.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chittor and Rana Kumbha:
1. The Vijaya Stambha commemorates Rana Kumbha's victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
2. The Kumbhalgarh fort was built by Rana Kumbha.
3. The Jain Kirti Stambha, built by the merchant Jijaji in the 12th century, is dedicated to Mahavira.
4. Rana Kumbha wrote the Sangeet Raj on music.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 4) are correct. 3 is wrong: Jijaji's Jain Kirti Stambha is dedicated to Adinath.

s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Bisaldeva Raso | i. Dalpati Vijay
b. Khuman Raso | ii. Narapati Nalha
c. Lalita Vigraharaja | iii. Somadeva
d. Hammir Mahakavya | iv. Nayachandra Suri
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Bisaldeva Raso – Narapati Nalha; Khuman Raso – Dalpati Vijay (not Karnidan); Lalita Vigraharaja – Somadeva; Hammir Mahakavya – Nayachandra Suri.

s:
Consider the following statements about Nagara sub-styles:
1. The Latina (Rekha-prasada) type has a single curvilinear tower.
2. The Valabhi type has a sloping, stepped roof.
3. The Maru-Gurjara style is associated with the Chandelas.
4. The Kirti-torana is a feature of the Maru-Gurjara style.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: Valabhi is barrel-vaulted; the sloping, stepped roof is Phamsana. 3 is wrong: Maru-Gurjara belongs to the Solankis of Gujarat-Rajasthan.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Rajput states failed to put up a combined opposition to the Turks.
Reason (R): Rajput warfare emphasised personal valour in direct, face-to-face combat.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the lack of a combined front came from constant feuds among the Rajput states, not from their style of warfare.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rajput society:
1. Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights.
2. In R.S. Sharma's 'Indian feudalism', vishti meant forced labour.
3. Jauhar was the self-immolation of women to avoid capture.
4. Rani Padmini's jauhar at Chittor was against Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 3) are correct. 4 is wrong: Rani Padmini's jauhar was against Alauddin Khalji.

s:
Match List-I (Chronicle) with List-II (Related fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Taj-ul-Maasir | i. Written at the Bahmani court c. 1350
b. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri | ii. Earliest reference to the magnetic compass in Indian seas
c. Futuh-us-Salatin | iii. Dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud
d. Jawami-ul-Hikayat | iv. Patron Qutbuddin Aibak
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Taj-ul-Maasir (Hasan Nizami) – patron Aibak; Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (Minhaj-us-Siraj) – dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud; Futuh-us-Salatin (Isami) – Bahmani court c. 1350; Jawami-ul-Hikayat (Aufi) – earliest reference to the magnetic compass.

s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Khazain-ul-Futuh | i. Amir Khusrau
b. Futuh-us-Salatin | ii. Abdul Malik Isami
c. Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi | iii. Yahya bin Ahmad Sarhindi
d. Fawaid-ul-Fawad | iv. Amir Hasan Sijzi
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Khazain-ul-Futuh – Amir Khusrau (Alauddin's campaigns); Futuh-us-Salatin – Isami; Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi – Yahya bin Ahmad Sarhindi; Fawaid-ul-Fawad – Amir Hasan Sijzi (conversations of Nizamuddin Auliya).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Minhaj-us-Siraj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri comprises 23 volumes.
2. The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was translated into English by Edward Sachau.
3. Besides Barani, Shams-i-Siraj Afif also wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
4. Barani's Fatawa-i-Jahandari is a work on the political theory of kingship.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was translated by H.G. Raverty; Sachau translated Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind.

s:
Match List-I (Later work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Tabaqat-i-Akbari | i. Badauni
b. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh | ii. Nizamuddin Ahmad
c. Muntakhab-ul-Lubab | iii. Firishta
d. Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi | iv. Khafi Khan
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari – Nizamuddin Ahmad (not Badauni); Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh – Badauni; Muntakhab-ul-Lubab – Khafi Khan (Aurangzeb's conquest of Golconda); Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi (Tarikh-i-Firishta) – Firishta.

s:
Consider the following statements about Firishta's history:
1. It was dedicated to Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda.
2. It calls Telangana 'Tilang'.
3. Its story of Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal is rejected by modern historians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Tarikh-i-Firishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) was dedicated to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur.

s:
Match List-I (Traveller) with List-II (Ruler at the time of the visit):
List-I | List-II
a. Nicolo Conti | i. Bahmani Muhammad Shah III
b. Abdur Razzaq | ii. Deva Raya II
c. Domingo Paes | iii. Deva Raya I
d. Afanasy Nikitin | iv. Krishnadeva Raya
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Nicolo Conti – Vijayanagara c. 1420 under Deva Raya I; Abdur Razzaq (envoy of Shah Rukh) – Deva Raya II, 1443-44; Domingo Paes – c. 1520, Krishnadeva Raya; Afanasy Nikitin – Bahmani kingdom under Muhammad Shah III.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ibn Battuta:
1. His Rihla was written in Persian.
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq made him Qazi of Delhi.
3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent him as envoy to Persia.
4. He described espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (2 and 4) are correct. 1 is wrong: the Rihla is in Arabic. 3 is wrong: he was sent as envoy to China.

s:
Consider the following statements about Marco Polo:
1. He came from Venice.
2. He landed at Motupalli in 1292.
3. He visited Andhra during the reign of Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: he came in Rudramadevi's reign – the first foreign reference to a female ruler in India.

s:
Match List-I (Traveller) with List-II (Country of origin):
List-I | List-II
a. Duarte Barbosa | i. Venice
b. Tavernier | ii. Portugal
c. Afanasy Nikitin | iii. France
d. Niccolao Manucci | iv. Russia
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Duarte Barbosa – Portugal; Tavernier – France (a jeweller, not Dutch); Afanasy Nikitin – Russia (Tver); Manucci – Venice.

s:
Consider the following statements about Al-Biruni:
1. He was a native of Khwarazm, in present Uzbekistan.
2. He wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic around 1030.
3. He recorded Diwali as falling on Kartika Purnima.
4. He was the first Muslim scholar to study the Puranas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 4) are correct. 3 is wrong: he recorded Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.

s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Rajatarangini | i. Gangadevi
b. Ramacharitam | ii. Sandhyakara Nandi
c. Madhura Vijayam | iii. Ali bin Tahir Bustani
d. Hadikat-us-Salatin | iv. Kalhana
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Rajatarangini – Kalhana; Ramacharitam – Sandhyakara Nandi; Madhura Vijayam – Gangadevi; Hadikat-us-Salatin – Ali bin Tahir Bustani (Qutb Shahis).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Madhura Vijayam describes conditions in Madurai under Tughlaq (Madurai Sultanate) rule before Kampana's conquest.
2. Kalhana's Rajatarangini has ten tarangas.
3. Ramacharitam tells the Ramayana together with the story of the Pala king Ramapala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Rajatarangini has eight tarangas.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Nastaliq script was used for Persian texts.
2. Quranic verses in Qutb Shahi buildings were written in Nastaliq.
3. The Golconda school of painting was founded by Mir Hashimi.
4. The Golconda manuscript 'Quliyat Quli' contains 23 miniatures.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: Quranic verses were written in Naskh. 4 is wrong: Quliyat Quli has 14 miniatures.

s:
Match List-I (Record) with List-II (What it tells us):
List-I | List-II
a. Palam Baoli inscription (1276) | i. Calls Balban 'Helper of the Caliph'
b. Nizami Mosque inscription, Golconda | ii. Dates Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence to 1518
c. Vilasa copper plate | iii. Praises Balban in Sanskrit
d. Garhmukteshwar mosque inscription | iv. Issued by Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Palam Baoli (1276) – praises Balban in Sanskrit; Nizami Mosque, Golconda – Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence in 1518; Vilasa copper plate (c. 1330) – Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; Garhmukteshwar mosque – Balban as 'Helper of the Caliph'.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Mahmud of Ghazni's Lahore dirhams are especially valuable as bilingual sources.
Reason (R): The coins of Iltutmish carried purely Arabic legends.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the dirhams matter because they carry an Arabic legend with its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script; Iltutmish's purely Arabic silver tanka and copper jital are a separate fact.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Babur's Tuzuk-i-Baburi was written in Turki.
2. Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama at Humayun's request.
3. The Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of the Akbarnama.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama at Akbar's request.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Telugu and Muslim sources agree that Warangal was invaded five times.
Reason (R): Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, went with Malik Kafur's 1310 Warangal campaign.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: Telugu sources (Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa, Kaluvacheru) count 8 invasions, Muslim sources (Khusrau, Wassaf) 5. R is true.

s:
Match List-I (Term at Balban's court) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Zil-i-Ilahi | i. Kissing the Sultan's feet
b. Sijda | ii. Prostration before the Sultan
c. Paibos | iii. A Persian festival
d. Nauroz | iv. Sultan as the shadow of God
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Zil-i-Ilahi – the Sultan as shadow of God; Sijda – prostration; Paibos – kissing the Sultan's feet; Nauroz – the Persian festival Balban introduced at court.

s:
Consider the following statements about Balban:
1. He rose from slave and water-carrier to member of the Forty and Amir-i-Shikar.
2. He served Nasiruddin Mahmud as naib (principal minister).
3. He broke the power of the Forty by promoting senior Turks.
4. He created the military department Diwan-i-Arz, separating it from the Diwan-i-Wizarat.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 4) are correct. 3 is wrong: Balban broke the Forty by promoting junior Turks.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Balban built outposts and forts on the frontier.
Reason (R): Balban kept the Mongols away by paying them tribute.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: Balban's defence against the Mongols relied on outposts and forts. R is false: there was no tribute; the forts were the defence.

s:
Consider the following statements about Iltutmish:
1. His regular Arabic coins were the silver tanka and the copper jital.
2. He received investiture ('mansur') from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229.
3. He defeated Tajuddin Yildiz at Tarain in 1216.
4. His rival Nasiruddin Qabacha held Badaun and Bhatinda.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 3) are correct. 4 is wrong: Nasiruddin Qabacha held Multan and Uch and fought Iltutmish for Lahore.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I | List-II
a. Turkan-i-Chahalgani | i. Tomb that made Iltutmish the 'Father of tomb building'
b. Iqta | ii. Turkish military elite ('the Forty')
c. Sultan Ghari | iii. Dedicated to Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki
d. Qutb Minar | iv. Revenue assignment in place of cash salary
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Turkan-i-Chahalgani – 'the Forty', a Turkish military elite (not Persian clerks); Iqta – revenue assignment held by muqtis; Sultan Ghari – the tomb that makes Iltutmish 'Father of tomb building'; Qutb Minar – dedicated to Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Chengiz Khan's Mongols turned back from the Indus in 1221.
Reason (R): Iltutmish refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni of Khwarazm, whom they were chasing.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: by refusing shelter to Mangbarni, Iltutmish gave the Mongols no cause to enter India, and they turned back.

s:
Consider the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak:
1. He was sold to the Qazi of Nishapur before becoming Muhammad Ghori's slave.
2. He held the office of Amir-i-Akhur (Master of Stables).
3. His capital was Delhi.
4. He was buried near Anarkali Bazaar in Lahore.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 4) are correct. 3 is wrong: Aibak's capital was Lahore; Iltutmish moved it to Delhi.

s:
Consider the following statements about the buildings and patronage of Qutbuddin Aibak:
1. He began the Quwwat-ul-Islam, the first mosque in Delhi.
2. He was the patron of Minhaj-us-Siraj.
3. He built the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Aibak was the patron of Hasan Nizami (Taj-ul-Maasir); Minhaj-us-Siraj dedicated his work to Nasiruddin Mahmud.

s:
Consider the following statements about Razia Sultan:
1. She discarded purdah, wore male attire and led the army.
2. The Turkish nobles resented her favour to Yaqut, a Persian.
3. Altuniya, who revolted against her in 1240, was governor of Bhatinda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Yaqut was an Abyssinian.

s:
Consider the following statements about the lines of the Mamluk dynasty:
1. The Qutbi line was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak.
2. The First Ilbari line was founded by Balban.
3. The Second Ilbari line (1266-1290) was founded by Balban.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: Iltutmish founded the First Ilbari line (1211-1266); Balban founded the Second Ilbari line.

s:
Match List-I (Mamluk ruler) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Nasiruddin Mahmud | i. Grandson and successor of Balban
b. Ruknuddin Firuz | ii. Succeeded Iltutmish in 1236
c. Kaiqubad | iii. Last ruler of the dynasty
d. Kaimurs | iv. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is named after him; preceded Balban
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66) – Tabaqat-i-Nasiri; ruled before Balban; Ruknuddin Firuz – succeeded Iltutmish; Kaiqubad – Balban's grandson and successor; infant Kaimurs – the last Mamluk.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at Badaun in 1290.
Reason (R): The Khaljis succeeded the Mamluks on the throne of Delhi.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: Jalaluddin crowned himself at Kilokhari (1290). R is true: his coronation began the Khalji dynasty.

s:
Match List-I (Mongol attack in Alauddin's reign) with List-II (Mongol leader):
List-I | List-II
a. Battle of Kili (1299) | i. Qutlugh Khwaja
b. Siege of Delhi (1303) | ii. Targhi
c. Amroha (1305) | iii. Ali Beg and Tartaq
d. Ravi (1306) | iv. Kabak
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kili (1299) – Qutlugh Khwaja; siege of Delhi (1303) – Targhi; Amroha (1305) – Ali Beg and Tartaq; Ravi (1306) – Kabak, beaten by Kafur and Ghazi Malik.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's defence against the Mongols:
1. During the siege of 1303 he sheltered in the Siri fort.
2. Ghazi Malik, warden of the marches, is said to have beaten the Mongols 18 times.
3. After 1306 the Ravi became the boundary between the Sultanate and the Mongols.
4. He maintained a large standing army and repaired the north-western forts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: Ghazi Malik is said to have beaten the Mongols 29 times.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Zafar Khan was killed fighting the Mongols at Kili in 1299.
Reason (R): Nusrat Khan was killed during the siege of Ranthambore.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Zafar Khan died at Kili against Qutlugh Khwaja's Mongols; Nusrat Khan's death at Ranthambore is a separate event.

s:
Consider the following statements about Malik Kafur:
1. He was seized at Cambay by Nusrat Khan during the Gujarat campaign of 1299.
2. He rose to be the Ariz-i-Mumalik of Alauddin.
3. He was called 'Hazar Dinari' because his first master had bought him for 1,000 dinars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the eunuch Kafur rose to Malik Naib.

s:
Match List-I (Kingdom attacked by Malik Kafur) with List-II (Ruler):
List-I | List-II
a. Devagiri (1307-08) | i. Ramachandra
b. Warangal (1309-10) | ii. Vira Pandya
c. Dwarasamudra (1310-11) | iii. Vira Ballala III
d. Madurai (1311) | iv. Prataparudra II
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Devagiri – Yadava Ramachandra; Warangal – Kakatiya Prataparudra II (not Shankaradeva); Dwarasamudra – Hoysala Vira Ballala III; Madurai – Vira Pandya.

s:
Consider the following statements about Kakatiya–Delhi relations:
1. The first attack on Warangal (1303) under Malik Fakhruddin Juna failed at Upparapalli.
2. Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna were the Kakatiya victors of 1303.
3. Malik Kafur besieged Warangal in 1309-10 together with Ulugh Khan.
4. Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Warangal as a single mud wall without a moat.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 2) are correct. 3 is wrong: Kafur's companion in 1309-10 was Khwaja Haji. 4 is wrong: Khusrau describes a double-walled fort with a moat.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Khusrau Khan led the third invasion of Warangal in 1318, under Mubarak Shah.
Reason (R): Kakatiya tribute to Delhi under the 1309-10 treaty had stopped after 1316.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: the tribute stopped after 1316, so Mubarak Shah sent Khusrau Khan against Warangal in 1318.

s:
Match List-I (Kingdom conquered by Alauddin) with List-II (Ruler):
List-I | List-II
a. Gujarat | i. Rana Ratan Singh
b. Ranthambore | ii. Mahlak Deva
c. Chittor | iii. Hammir Deva
d. Malwa | iv. Rai Karan (Karnadeva II)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Gujarat (1299) – Vaghela Rai Karan; Ranthambore (1301) – Hammir Deva Chauhan; Chittor (1303) – Rana Ratan Singh; Malwa (1305) – Mahlak Deva.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign:
1. It took place in 1301.
2. It was led by Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan.
3. The Vaghela queen Kamala Devi was captured in it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Gujarat was conquered in 1299 – the first of Alauddin's conquests.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's conquests:
1. Nusrat Khan was killed during the first siege of Ranthambore.
2. Ain-ul-Mulk Multani conquered Malwa in 1305.
3. Shital Deva of Siwana was defeated during the campaigns in Rajputana.
4. The southern kingdoms were annexed and made provinces.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 3) are correct. 4 is wrong: in the south the kings kept their thrones and paid tribute; only the north was annexed.

s:
Match List-I (Name / post of Alauddin) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Ali Gurshasp | i. Army minister
b. Amir-i-Tuzuk | ii. The Second Alexander
c. Ariz-i-Mumalik | iii. Master of ceremonies
d. Sikandar-i-Sani | iv. His name before he became Sultan
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Ali Gurshasp – his earlier name; Amir-i-Tuzuk – master of ceremonies and Ariz-i-Mumalik – army minister (posts under Jalaluddin); Sikandar-i-Sani – 'Second Alexander', on his coins.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's kingship:
1. He told Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana that he acted in the interest of the state.
2. He revived the harsh, centralised rule of Balban, without religious sanction.
3. He dropped his plans of world conquest and a new religion on the advice of Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk.
4. Barani separated the Shariat from the Zawabit, the state laws made by the ruler.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four are correct: he told Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana he acted in the interest of the state, revived Balban's harsh centralised rule without religious sanction, dropped world conquest and a new religion on Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk's advice, and Barani separated Shariat from Zawabit.

s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Khaljis:
1. After Alauddin's death Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar.
2. Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, the last Khalji, was murdered by Malik Kafur.
3. In 1320 Ghazi Malik killed Khusrau Khan and became Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Kafur himself was killed; Mubarak Shah was murdered by Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah).

s:
Consider the following statements about Jalaluddin Khalji:
1. He crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290 at about the age of 50.
2. He was lenient to rebels such as Malik Chhajju.
3. He married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Timur.
4. Mongol converts were settled in his reign as 'New Mussalmans'.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (2 and 4) are correct. 1 is wrong: he was about 70 when he crowned himself at Kilokhari. 3 is wrong: Ulugh Khan was a descendant of Chengiz Khan.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chittor and the Padmini legend:
1. Alauddin took Chittor from Rana Ratan Singh in 1303.
2. Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat in Persian in 1540.
3. Padmavat was written more than two centuries after the conquest of Chittor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Padmavat (1540) is in Awadhi (early Hindi), not Persian.

s:
Match List-I (Market of Alauddin Khalji) with List-II (Goods):
List-I | List-II
a. Mandi | i. Food grains
b. Sarai Adl | ii. Cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil
c. Third market | iii. Miscellaneous goods
d. Fourth market | iv. Horses, slaves and cattle
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Alauddin set up four markets: Mandi – food grains; Sarai Adl – cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter, oil; the third – horses, slaves, cattle; the fourth – miscellaneous goods.

s:
Match List-I (Official / department) with List-II (Role):
List-I | List-II
a. Shahna-i-Mandi | i. Recovery of revenue arrears from officials
b. Diwan-i-Riyasat | ii. Ran the whole market system
c. Munhiyan | iii. Secret spies sending daily reports
d. Diwan-i-Mustakhraj | iv. Superintendent of each market
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Shahna-i-Mandi – superintendent of a market (e.g. Malik Kabool); Diwan-i-Riyasat – the whole market system, under the Naib-i-Riyasat; Munhiyan – secret spies; Diwan-i-Mustakhraj – recovery of arrears.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's market control:
1. Its plan aimed at fixed prices, sure supply, controlled distribution and the end of monopolies.
2. One of its aims was to pay lower wages to the palace artisans.
3. State granaries released grain in times of shortage.
4. Slave boys were used to make test purchases.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: the aim was to let a large, low-paid standing army live on fixed low prices – not lower wages for palace artisans.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue terms:
1. Ghari was a grazing tax on milch cattle.
2. Charai was a house tax.
3. Kismat-i-khuti, the headman's cess, was abolished.
4. Biswa was the unit of land measurement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (3 and 4) are correct. 1 and 2 are interchanged: Ghari was the house tax and Charai the grazing tax on milch cattle.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji forbade nobles to hold feasts or make marriage alliances without his permission.
Reason (R): Barani names the nobles' intermarriages and gatherings as one cause of revolts.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: the ordinance on feasts and marriage alliances was aimed at the gatherings and intermarriages that Barani saw as breeding revolt.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's ordinances:
1. A weak spy system was one of the causes of revolt he perceived, so he reorganised the spies.
2. He confiscated the nobles' property, religious grants and free lands.
3. He prohibited liquor, intoxicants and gambling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Barani lists the nobles' wealth, the weak spy system, drinking and the nobles' gatherings as causes, and an ordinance met each.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's military reforms:
1. Dagh was the branding of horses and huliya (chehra) the descriptive roll of soldiers.
2. The Ariz-i-Mamalik headed revenue collection.
3. The Bahmani minister Mahmud Gawan later copied dagh and chehra.
4. The soldiers of the standing army were paid through iqtas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: the Ariz-i-Mamalik handled army administration. 4 is wrong: the standing army was paid in cash from the treasury.

s:
Consider the following statements about the dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. Token currency, the transfer of the capital and canals are associated with the Tughlaqs.
2. Agra was founded by the Tughlaqs.
3. The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Agra was founded by the Lodis.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ziauddin Barani's Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is the main source for Alauddin's market control.
2. Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Alauddin's campaigns.
3. Alauddin's price controls were abolished by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20) abolished price control and restored the confiscated lands.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji's controls were enforced uniformly across the whole empire.
Reason (R): Espionage and repression under Alauddin bred discontent among merchants and peasants.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: the controls were largely confined to Delhi. R is true: espionage and repression bred discontent.

s:
Match List-I (Institution of Firoz Shah Tughlaq) with List-II (Function):
List-I | List-II
a. Diwan-i-Khairat | i. Pensions and grants to deserving persons
b. Diwan-i-Bandagan | ii. Charity
c. Dar-ul-Shifa | iii. Department of slaves
d. Diwan-i-Istihqaq | iv. Free hospital
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Diwan-i-Khairat – charity (orphans, widows, marriages of poor girls); Diwan-i-Bandagan – slaves (about 1,80,000); Dar-ul-Shifa – free hospital; Diwan-i-Istihqaq – pensions and grants.

s:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's welfare measures:
1. His kotwals listed the unemployed, who were given jobs by merit.
2. He laid out about 1,200 gardens and orchards near Delhi.
3. He retained mutilation (cutting of hands and feet) as a punishment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Firoz banned mutilation.

s:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canals:
1. He built the largest network of canals among the Delhi Sultans.
2. His irrigation cess, haq-i-sharb, was one-fifth of the produce.
3. His canal from the Yamuna to Hisar was about 150 miles long.
4. His Rajabwah canal was restored under Akbar as the Shihab Canal.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: haq-i-sharb was one-tenth of the produce of fields watered by royal canals.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I | List-II
a. Fatehabad | i. Firoz's own account (autobiography)
b. Jaunpur | ii. Town founded in memory of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
c. Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi | iii. Town named after Firoz's son Fateh Khan
d. Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi | iv. Persian translation of the Jawalamukhi Sanskrit manuscripts
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Fatehabad – named after Fateh Khan; Jaunpur – in memory of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Jauna Khan); Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi – Azizuddin Khalid Khani's translation of the Nagarkot (Jawalamukhi) manuscripts; Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi – Firoz's autobiography.

s:
Match List-I (Experiment of Muhammad bin Tughlaq) with List-II (Result):
List-I | List-II
a. Higher taxation of the Doab | i. Peasant revolts and flight
b. Token currency | ii. Mass forgery
c. Khurasan expedition | iii. Army destroyed in the hills
d. Qarachil expedition | iv. Army disbanded unpaid
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Doab taxation (c. 1326) coincided with famine – revolts and flight; token currency (1329-30) – mass forgery; Khurasan (1332) – army of 3,70,000 disbanded unpaid; Qarachil (1333) – army destroyed in the Kumaon hills.

s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. He moved the capital from Delhi to Devagiri (Daulatabad) in 1327.
2. His silver coin was called the Dinar.
3. His token coins were of copper and brass, on the model of Kublai Khan's paper money.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: his silver coin was the Adli; the Dinar was his gold coin.

s:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi | i. State loans for seeds and wells
b. Taqavi (sondhar) | ii. Famine-relief camp on the Ganga near Kannauj
c. Swarga-dwari | iii. Department to bring waste land under cultivation
d. Uluq | iv. Royal horse couriers every four miles
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi – MBT's agriculture department for waste land; Taqavi (sondhar) – loans for seeds and wells; Swarga-dwari – famine-relief camp near Kannauj; Uluq – horse couriers every four miles (dawa – foot couriers).

s:
Consider the following statements about Ibn Battuta:
1. He was born at Tangiers.
2. He arrived in India in 1342.
3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq made him Qazi of Delhi and sent him as envoy to China.
4. He noted that sati was completely prohibited in the Sultanate.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: he arrived in 1333; 1342 is when he left Delhi for China as envoy. 4 is wrong: he noted that sati needed the Sultan's permission – it was not prohibited.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Barani wrote the Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi.
2. Badauni remarked on Muhammad bin Tughlaq's death that 'the king was freed from his people and they from their king'.
3. Barani called Muhammad bin Tughlaq a 'mixture of opposites'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Barani wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari; the Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is Firoz's own account.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq:
1. As Ghazi Malik he was Governor of Punjab under Alauddin Khalji.
2. He limited any increase in land revenue to about one-tenth.
3. Warangal fell to his forces in 1323 after a five-month siege and was renamed Sultanpur.
4. The Kakatiya Prataparudra II died in the Godavari on the way to Delhi.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (1, 2 and 3) are correct. 4 is wrong: Prataparudra II died in the Narmada.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq replaced Alauddin's measurement on khalisa land with sharing of the crop (batai).
Reason (R): Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the first Sultan of Delhi to dig canals.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the shift from measurement to crop-sharing was a revenue choice; digging canals is a separate measure.

s:
Match List-I (State / event) with List-II (Leader):
List-I | List-II
a. Coastal Andhra freed (c. 1325) | i. Prolaya Vema Reddi
b. Madurai Sultanate (1335) | ii. Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah
c. Warangal recaptured (1336) | iii. Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah
d. Bahmani kingdom (1347) | iv. Kapaya Nayaka
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Coastal Andhra – Prolaya Vema Reddi (Reddis); Madurai Sultanate – Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah; Warangal recaptured – Kapaya Nayaka (Musunuri); Bahmani kingdom – Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Madurai Sultanate was established in 1335.
2. Madhura Vijayam, which describes Tughlaq rule in the South, was written by Tirumalamba.

Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq:
1. He was the uncle of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
2. He was placed on the throne at Thatta in 1351.
3. He abolished about 24 taxes and kept the four Islamic taxes.
4. He made the iqtas hereditary.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only three (2, 3 and 4) are correct. 1 is wrong: Firoz, son of Ghiyasuddin's brother Rajab, was MBT's cousin, not uncle.

Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Firoz Shah Tughlaq made jizya a separate tax and extended it to Brahmins.
Reason (R): Firoz Shah Tughlaq acted on the advice of the ulema.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: on the ulema's advice Firoz made jizya a separate tax and extended it to Brahmins.

Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's reign:
1. His expeditions to Bengal against Haji Iliyas were successful.
2. Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay him tribute.
3. His wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul paid compensation to the victims of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: both Bengal expeditions against Haji Iliyas failed (the second in 1359-60).

Match List-I (Sultan) with List-II (Distinctive measure):
List-I | List-II
a. Balban | i. The city of Tughlaqabad
b. Alauddin Khalji | ii. Zil-i-Ilahi theory, sijda and paibos
c. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq | iii. Dagh (branding of horses) and the city of Siri
d. Firoz Shah Tughlaq | iv. Canals, irrigation and public works
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Balban – Zil-i-Ilahi, sijda, paibos; Alauddin – dagh, huliya, Siri; Ghiyasuddin – Tughlaqabad; Firoz – canals and public works.

s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Tughlaqs:
1. Abu Bakr was one of the weak successors of Firoz after 1388.
2. Timur invaded India during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
3. The Tughlaq period is placed between 1320 and 1414.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Timur invaded in 1398, in the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah, the last Tughlaq.
